Agent Name: Planner  
Step Number: 6  
Reason for Mistake: The Planner incorrectly assumed that the 1967 Pan American Games used a 440-yard track (402.336 meters) instead of a standard 400-meter track. This led to the erroneous calculation of the number of laps as approximately 24.85 (rounded to 24 laps). However, the standard track length for international competitions had already transitioned to 400 meters by the time of the 1967 Pan American Games, meaning the correct calculation should have been 10,000 / 400 = 25 laps. The Planner failed to verify the track length with authoritative sources before concluding the task.
